title: Headless commerce: integration boundaries
summary: Verify the custom storefront, Shopify checkout and external tools separately.
why: A flexible storefront may need its own app, tracking and consent integrations.
Clear data and route ownership prevents configuration in the wrong system.
know: The XTERRA snapshot uses Astro for the storefront, Sanity for marketing content, and Shopify for products, cart and hosted checkout.
Verify checkout/order integrations, custom browsing/form events and email flows separately.
Implement SEO and redirects at the domain and routing layer receiving old URLs. Shopify redirect imports alone may not affect Astro.
Custom consent choices may not reach Shopify, analytics or marketing. Test cross-domain behavior, withdrawal and rejection.
Shopify Dev MCP provides documentation and validation; it does not grant store read/write access. Check each account and API scope.
inputs: Repository/commit, storefront/checkout domains and deployment environments
Data sources, event and integration owners, app support and secure connections
actions: Map data, events, domains and owners. Check each app’s headless APIs, webhooks and limits.
Test product updates, cart/discounts, checkout return, order events, form-to-CRM and retries separately.
Test old URLs at the real routing layer. Verify production canonicals, indexing controls and feed URLs.
Resolve the XTERRA README/Klaviyo-document discrepancy using code and account evidence before changing anything. Do not reinstall integrations or activate drafts by assumption.
done: Data and events are traceable without duplicates; unknown hosted settings are explicit gaps.
Handoff covers domains, ownership and failures. A successful Git push does not prove customer availability.
pitfalls: Applying theme instructions to a custom frontend.
Treating repository descriptions as proof of live flows or orders.
decision: Agree on system responsibilities and cutover scope to avoid duplicate implementations.

reader.concept: Headless commerce separates the storefront from transactions. The frontend handles browsing; Shopify handles products, cart and checkout.
reader.when: Use this for a custom frontend such as Astro or an app that does not appear after installation.

example.situation: Shopify tracking is configured, but custom product pages send no view or cart events.
example.lesson: Check storefront, checkout and external tools separately.

reader.first_step: Map the storefront, CMS, Shopify and external-tool responsibilities.
terms: The site customers browse and use.
Checkout provided and managed by Shopify.
An API exposes operations; scopes limit what a connection can access.
